title: Fidelity scorecard
description: One boundary's fidelity result for one (subject, mode, fixture set). Three properties are enforced here rather than left to discipline. (1) Every gate metric MUST carry `mean`, `worst_layer`, `worst_head` and `worst_row`: the worst-layer mandate comes from SageAttention's 99.70% average against a 56.40% worst layer, and worst-ROW from the 2026-08-30 addendum, where a per-tensor scheme's depth collapse (cosine 0.894 -> 0.049) was invisible in the mean AND in the worst-head aggregate. (2) Every value is anchored to a control measured on the same tensors in the same process, so the record carries a ratio and never a bare absolute. (3) `norm_ratio` is structurally un-gateable (`gated` is `const false`), per addendum item 2: it drifts informatively with depth but never leaves [0.98, 1.02], so a gate on it would never fire and a trend line is what is worth keeping.

scorecard_id.description: Stable name for this scorecard. Conventionally <subject>-<mode>-<fixture_set_id>-<boundary>.

boundary.description: Which of the plan's three boundaries this scorecard measures. Boundaries have different saturation risks and are never mixed in one record.

status.description: `draft` until the tier that owns the lane has confirmed it. A public-lane 4090 result backing a private-lane envelope is `draft` by construction.

impl.description: What was measured, in the harness's own vocabulary (e.g. `attn_kernel_lab.ops.prefill_extend`).

loaded_from.description: Which artifact the operator actually loaded -- `jit`, `wheel`, or whatever the loader reports. A fidelity number is about the binary that ran, and the loader has a precedence order, so the record states which side of it won rather than inferring it from the source digest.

env_switches.description: Every switch that changes numerics and survives into production. Contract §7 leaves their status open, which is exactly why they are recorded per scorecard: a mode-specific failure is diagnosed here first (plan §8).

controls.description: The anchors. At least one must be the implementation swap whose values populate every metric block's `control` field; the harness floor assertions ride here too.

primary.description: True on the single control whose per-slice values fill `control` in every metric block.

slice_semantics.description: What a `layer` and a `row` ARE in this fixture set. The public synthetic lane has no model, so its layer axis is the fixture case; the private lane's is the model's full-attention layer id. Saying so in the record is what stops a public worst-layer number from being read as a model-layer number.

environment.description: Determinism prerequisites of plan §4.2 are enforced here, not asserted in prose: a TF32-contaminated FP32 reference is not one, and the true-FP32 rotation is reproducible only under the contract §3.1 workspace pin.

not_claimed.description: Required. A fidelity number that travels without its scope statement becomes a quality claim in one retelling; upstream/CLAIMS.md forbids `quality-neutral` in any form and this field is where that survives the copy-paste.

gate_metric.description: A metric admitted to the gate. All four aggregations are required: an average-only scorecard would have passed the 56.40%-worst-layer kernel, and a worst-head-only scorecard would have passed the cosine-0.049 worst row.

ratio_basis.description: How the ratio is formed. `direct` is value/control. `one_minus` anchors a similarity through its deficit, (1-value)/(1-control): the ratio of two cosines both near 1 is ~1 for any pair and would report a collapse as agreement.

saturated.description: control >= 0.5 * value on the ratio basis. A saturated metric is demoted to a smoke check and may not rank backends (plan §1).

reported_metric.description: Reported, never gated. `gated` is `const false` so the addendum's rule cannot be quietly reversed by an author who wants a threshold.
